pages.observed: Option a frames 0 to 24. Flat illustrated airport curb under a canopy. Phone overlay upper left shows a route map with Ride requested and Finding a car. A white sensor-roofed SUV slides in from the left edge toward an empty chevron pickup bay. Caption from 0.2 s reads Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a Waymo with no driver, over the road. Lower half of frame is empty gray asphalt.

Option a 1.0 to 1.8 s. Same airport curb wide shot. The white sensor-roofed SUV slides further right and settles inside the painted pickup bay with a red glow at its rear lamp. Phone overlay still reads Ride requested, Finding a car. Caption unchanged. Car occupies a small band at mid-frame; lower half remains empty asphalt.

Option a 2.0 to 2.8 s. Car parked in bay at the curb with red rear glow while a small Texas outline card appears at top right. At 2.6 s the shot cuts to the car interior seen from the back: steering wheel, dash map screen, two empty front seats, windshield showing the airport sign. Phone overlay stays at upper left; caption sits across the lower seat area.

Option a 3.0 to 3.8 s. Interior view from behind the empty front seats. The steering wheel turns with no hands on it: its tan marker moves clockwise. The blue airport sign slides out past the right edge of the windshield. The locator card draws the Texas outline. The steering wheel occupies a small area in the middle third; seats fill the lower half behind the caption.

Option a 4.0 to 4.8 s. Same interior view held. Steering wheel stays turned with its marker at the right. Only the edge of the blue airport sign remains visible at the windshield's right border. Texas locator outline is complete. Phone overlay still shows Ride requested, Finding a car. No visible new change across these five samples.

Option a 5.0 to 5.8 s. Interior shot ends with caption clearing at 5.2 s. At 5.4 s a closer curb shot shows a large tilted phone in front of the parked white SUV, which sits beside the blue airport sign. Phone still reads Ride requested and Finding a car; no visible change to arriving in these samples. Caption reads the airport included. Locator card shows a ring near San Antonio.

Option a 6.0 to 6.8 s. Same curb close shot with the large phone in front of the parked white SUV. The phone's car marker moves to the destination pin and the status text changes from Ride requested to Arriving, At the curb at 6.2 s. Caption the airport included clears by 6.6 s. Car itself does not move in these samples.

Option a 7.0 to 7.8 s. Cut to a pale paper street map lying on a wooden table, with a February calendar page standing at its top right edge and three tiny pins near the center. Map grid is faint. By 7.8 s a blue river line starts drawing across the map. Disclosure card still reads Generic car with no brand mark. Lower third of frame is plain table planks.

Option a 8.0 to 8.8 s. Same map table shot. A blue river line extends top to bottom through the map and faint gray highway lines and a ring road draw in around the three central pins. The Texas locator card fades away at 8.0 s. February calendar page stays put. Map lines are thin and low contrast at phone size.

Option a 9.0 to 9.8 s. Cut to a closer view of the map. A tag reading 60 square miles, Limited area pins at the top center. A February calendar page slides in from the right and lands on the lower right corner of the map. A black outline line starts tracing from the upper left. Caption reads in a limited area of sixty square miles.

Option a 10.0 to 10.8 s. Close map view. A black outline line continues tracing clockwise from the top of the map down the right side, around the pins, while the 60 square miles tag stays pinned at top. The February calendar page settles at the lower left of the map. Outline not closed yet at 10.8 s. Caption unchanged.

Option a 11.0 to 11.8 s. The black outline completes into a closed irregular polygon around the three pins and the river at 11.2 s, then fills with translucent gray. The 60 square miles tag and February page remain. The zone sits in the upper middle of the frame above the caption.

Option a 12.0 to 12.8 s. Completed map state held: closed gray zone with three pins, 60 square miles tag and February page. The pin markers shift a few pixels inside the zone. Caption clears at 12.8 s. No car pin visibly riding from the curb is identifiable; pins are small circles.

Option a 13.0 to 13.8 s. Cut at 13.2 s to a wide flooded creek: brown water fills most of the frame, a white SUV sits in the water near stacked limestone ledges at the right, a large tree and brush on the far bank. The disclosure now reads A different car, April 20th account. The car shifts a short distance left away from the ledge by 13.6 s. Caption In April, an empty Waymo was swept into Salado Creek. Car is small, occupying about a third of frame width.

Option a 14.0 to 14.8 s. Same wide creek shot. The white car sits in brown water left of the limestone ledges with water at its lower doors. A brown mound of water builds against its right side by 14.6 s. The car drifts only slightly left. Cabin windows are light gray; occupancy not distinguishable at this scale. Caption unchanged.

Option a 15.0 to 15.8 s. The car drifts further left with a brown bow wave pushing against its right side. At 15.4 s a match cut moves to a closer framing of the same creek without the ledges. The car tilts and sinks deeper, water reaching the window line, and continues moving left across 15.6 to 15.8 s. Car occupies about a third of frame width above the caption band.

Option a 16.0 to 16.8 s. The car is sunk to its window line in the brown creek with a wave crest and floating debris trailing to its right. Its position on screen changes little across these samples. Dark rounded shapes show through the side windows; at this scale they could read as seat backs or as heads. Caption unchanged. Car is small, about a quarter of frame width.

Option a 17.0 to 17.8 s. The submerged car slides left until it is cut off by the left frame edge at 17.4 s. At 17.6 s a cut to a flooded residential street: a white sensor-roofed SUV stands in brown water to its lower body in front of two tan houses, a tree, a fence and a green street sign. A dark gray blob sits at the right edge. The lower third is pale sidewalk tiles. Disclosure reads Another car, earlier in April.

Option a 18.0 to 18.8 s. The white SUV rolls slowly right along the flooded street while the brown water climbs from its wheels up past the wheel arches, hiding the lower wheels by 18.8 s. Caption Earlier that month, another empty car was stranded in floodwater. The car sits just above the caption band and is about a third of frame width.

Option a 19.0 to 19.8 s. The white SUV holds still in the flooded street with water covering its wheels. From 19.6 s small amber lamp glows appear at its front and rear corners. The lamps are small relative to the frame. Caption unchanged.

Option a 20.0 to 20.8 s. A closer side view of the stopped white SUV standing in brown floodwater above the wheel rims, its reflection below. Amber corner lamps glow at 20.2 and 20.4 s and are dim at the other samples, so they appear to blink. Windows show seat headrest shapes and no visible person. Car occupies about two thirds of frame width just above the caption.

Option a 21.0 to 21.8 s. Same close side view of the stopped SUV in brown floodwater. Corner lamps keep glowing on and off. Water surface and car position hold still. Windows show seat headrests with no person. Caption unchanged through the end of the scene.

Option a 22.0 to 22.8 s. Cut from the flooded street to an olive wall over a brown desk where a cream card headed Federal recall record, Vehicle safety recall slides in from the right with a pen resting at its lower right. By 22.8 s field text begins writing: Reca and Sof. The card is cropped at the right edge. Caption Waymo filed a software recall.

Option a 23.0 to 23.8 s. The record card settles centered on the desk and its rows type in: Recall type, Software, then Potential units affected, 3,791. A text cursor follows the typing. Pen remains at lower right. The card fills about two thirds of the width in the middle band of the frame; the upper third is plain olive wall.

Option a 24.0 to 24.8 s. Completed record card holds, caption clears at 24.4 s. At 24.6 s the framing shifts: the card moves to the top of the frame and a grid of faint outlined car slots appears on the desk below. By 24.8 s the first three slots fill with white car icons. Caption that could affect nearly thirty eight hundred cars.

Option a 25.0 to 25.8 s. The card sits at the top while the icon grid below fills row by row with small white car icons until almost all five rows are full. From 25.4 s a hand and forearm in a blue sleeve enter from the right holding a wooden stamp and carry it over the card's upper area by 25.8 s. Grid icons are tiny at phone size.

Option a 26.0 to 26.8 s. The grid is full. A hand in a blue sleeve hovers a wooden stamp over the card, then presses it down at 26.8 s leaving an amber-bordered mark whose visible text begins So, partly hidden by the stamp. A tag reading Nearly 3,800 vehicles, 3,791 potentially affected in the record drops in tilted between card and grid and straightens. Small type on the tag is very small at phone size.

Option a 27.0 to 27.8 s. The stamp lifts away revealing an amber Software recall stamp on the card; the hand withdraws off the right edge by 27.6 s. The completed layout holds: card with Software and 3,791, the Nearly 3,800 vehicles tag and the full grid of car icons. Caption unchanged.

Option a 28.0 to 28.8 s. The record layout holds until a cut at 28.4 s to a flat side view of a multi-lane road with a lamp post, trees and skyline. The disclosure changes to The recall wording, not a recorded event. A white SUV enters from the left. At 28.8 s a faint quote card fades in above the road with the recall sentence. No water is visible yet. The road band occupies a thin middle strip; the lower half is grass.

Option a 29.0 to 29.8 s. The recall sentence card is fully visible above the road. The white SUV stays near the left-center while lane dashes and the lamp post slide left past it, so the car reads as driving right with the camera following. No standing water is visible yet. Car sits on the road band just above the caption.

Option a 30.0 to 30.8 s. The car keeps its screen position as the roadside scrolls left. A red brake glow shows at its rear from 30.2 s and brightens by 30.8 s. At 30.8 s the edge of a pale gray-blue water patch slides into view at the right edge of the road ahead of the car.

Option a 31.0 to 31.8 s. The car creeps right toward a pale gray water patch at the right edge of the road. Its red brake glow shows until about 31.4 s and is gone by 31.6 s. The water patch sits at the frame edge and its lower half overlaps the caption bar. The car and water are still separated by about a car length at 31.8 s.

Option a 32.0 to 32.8 s. The car keeps creeping right toward the pale water patch at the frame edge without reaching it. Caption clears at 32.6 s. At 32.8 s a cut to a close side view: the SUV fills about four fifths of the width on the lane, with a thin white wavy line along the road surface at its tires and the quote card above. Grass fills the lower half.

Option a 33.0 to 33.8 s. Close side view of the SUV filling most of the width. A pale gray water patch slides in from the right edge toward the front tire, reaching about a quarter of the way into the frame by 33.8 s. The car stays fixed on screen. A thin wavy white line runs along the road under both tires. Caption then drive into standing water on higher speed roads.

Option a 34.0 to 34.8 s. In the close side view the pale gray water sheet reaches the front tire and spreads under it, with small splash marks at the wheel by 34.8 s. The word may in the recall sentence turns amber from 34.2 s. The car stays fixed on screen while the water moves toward it. Water edge is pale and low contrast against the gray road.

Option a 35.0 to 35.8 s. The pale water sheet spreads under the whole car, with fanned wake lines and reflections at the front tire. The car body stays fixed on screen; motion is carried by the water and wake moving past it. The word may stays amber. Caption unchanged.

Option a 36.0 to 36.8 s. The car stands in the pale water sheet with wakes at both wheels while the background tree and post slide left. The highlighted may remains. Caption clears at 36.6 s. Water reaches only the tire bottoms; depth is not drawn above the rims.

Option a 37.0 to 37.8 s. Cut to the same recall record card, now taller with an empty lower section. From 37.4 s a Remedy row types in reading The remedy is currently under development, and its background lights pale amber by 37.8 s. Caption The federal record says the remedy is currently under development. Card occupies the upper middle; lower third is plain olive.

Option a 38.0 to 38.8 s. The remedy row stays lit. From 38.2 s a hand in a blue sleeve holding a pen enters from the right and brings the pen tip to rest just after the word currently on the remedy row by 38.6 s, then holds. Hand and pen are drawn with simple forms; forearm extends off the right edge.

Option a 39.0 to 39.8 s. With the pen hand still resting on the remedy row, a second arm in a blue sleeve enters from the lower right carrying a wooden stamp and positions it over the lower half of the remedy row. Both arms come from the right edge. The framing pushes in slightly at 39.2 s. The stamp has not landed by 39.8 s.

Option a 40.0 to 40.8 s. The stamp presses onto the lower part of the remedy row at 40.4 s, then lifts and moves down-right leaving an amber, slightly tilted Under development stamp mark under the remedy text. The pen hand stays resting on the row. Caption unchanged.

Option a 41.0 to 41.8 s. The pen and stamp hands withdraw to the right leaving the Under development stamp on the remedy row; caption clears. At 41.6 s a cut to a wet lot: four white sensor-roofed cars parked in a diagonal row under a wire strung between two poles, with a small vehicle map card hanging from the wire and an April calendar page on a pole. At 41.8 s a tag partly reading ther limits slides in from the left along the wire.

Option a 42.0 to 42.8 s. The tag slides along the wire and pins at upper left, now readable as Weather limits, tightened, with a cloud and rain icon. The four parked white cars below do not move. The vehicle map card and April page stay in place. Tags are small, roughly a fifth of frame width.

Option a 43.0 to 43.8 s. The Weather limits, tightened tag moves along the wire to the center and swings slightly. The parked row of four white cars stays unchanged. No car is marked or updated in these samples. Caption unchanged.

Option a 44.0 to 44.8 s. The lot composition holds: tag swaying slightly on the wire, four parked cars unchanged, April page and map card unchanged. Caption unchanged. Combined with 43.0 to 43.8 s, the cars do not change for about two seconds.

Option a 45.0 to 45.8 s. The wide lot holds, caption clears at 45.4 s. At 45.6 s a match cut to a lower, closer view: the front white car fills about three quarters of width with the row receding to the right, the Weather limits tag larger at upper left, map card and April page at right. Caption and every affected car had the update by April twentieth. No check marks yet.

Option a 46.0 to 46.8 s. Round check-mark badges appear above the cars one at a time from the front car toward the back of the row: front at 46.0 to 46.2 s, second at 46.4 s, third and fourth by 46.6 to 46.8 s. The badges shrink with distance. The April page still shows no date number in these samples.

Option a 47.0 to 47.8 s. All four visible cars carry check badges. A small check mark draws onto the Vehicle maps card at upper right by 47.4 s, with a tiny word under it. The April page still shows no visible 20. The frame then holds.

Option a 48.0 to 48.8 s. The checked row holds for about 0.6 s, then at 48.8 s the small calendar page at right flips to show a large 20 (the April header is mostly hidden by the flip). The calendar is small, at the right edge, about an eighth of frame width.

Option a 49.0 to 49.8 s. Completed state holds: all visible cars checked, map card checked, calendar reading April 20 at the right edge with the turned page settling above it. Caption clears at 49.8 s.

Option a 50.0 to 50.8 s. Cut back to the same airport curb wide framing as the opening, now with the white SUV already stopped in the bay and the phone overlay showing Arriving, At the curb. Disclosure reads A generic airport ride, not the flood cars. Caption So the airport ride is open. No door has opened in these samples.

Option a 51.0 to 51.8 s. In the curb wide shot the white SUV's rear side door swings open from 51.2 s and stays open, showing a dark interior gap. The car is small in frame, about a third of width, at mid-height. Caption So the airport ride is open.

Option a 52.0 to 52.8 s. The door stays open at the curb. Caption clears at 52.6 s. At 52.8 s the framing changes: the phone overlay is gone, a small phone rests on the bench, and a small recall card reading The remedy is currently under development with an Under development stamp sits on the dark road in front of the car. Card is small, about two fifths of frame width, and its text is very small at phone size.

Option a 53.0 to 53.8 s. The recall card rests on the road in the foreground between the car and the caption, tilting slightly and straightening. The SUV stays in the bay with its rear door open; the phone lies on the bench. The card's remedy text is small but its large words The remedy is currently under development are distinguishable. Caption and the federal record lists the flood remedy.

Option a 54.0 to 54.8 s. The recall card grows from small to about two thirds of frame width and slides up so its top edge overlaps the car's wheels, with the remedy row lit amber and the Under development stamp at bottom right. The SUV and open door remain visible above the card. Caption and the federal record lists the flood remedy.

Option a 55.0 to 55.8 s. The pairing holds: the recall card with its lit remedy row sits in front of and slightly overlapping the white SUV whose rear door stays open at the curb. Only small drift is visible. Caption unchanged.

Option a 56.0 to 56.8 s. After the caption clears, at 56.4 s the frame becomes a split: the upper half shows the white SUV at the curb with its rear door open beside the airport sign, the lower half a brown desk holding the recall card with the lit remedy row and Under development stamp, plus a small phone showing a route. Caption as currently under development.

Option a 57.0 to 57.8 s. The split holds: car with open door at the curb above, the recall card and phone on the desk below. A dark underline extends under the remedy text line from left to right across these samples. The lower third of the frame is plain desk below the caption.

Option a 58.0 to 58.8 s. The final split of car with open door above and the recall card on the desk below holds, caption clearing at 58.2 s. At 58.6 s a cut to a dark credits card: Texas Lone Star flag, Texas AI Docket wordmark, texasaidocket.com, and source, illustration, map and music credits.
Option a 59.0 to 59.8 s. The dark credits card holds unchanged: Lone Star flag, Texas AI Docket wordmark, Visit the Docket texasaidocket.com, and the sources, illustration, map and music credits.
Option a 60.0 to 60.8 s. The same dark credits card holds without change: flag, Texas AI Docket wordmark, texasaidocket.com and the credit lines.
Option a 61.0 to 61.8 s. The dark credits card continues to hold unchanged with the flag, wordmark, URL and credit lines.
Option a 62.0 to 62.8 s. The credits card holds unchanged: flag, Texas AI Docket wordmark, texasaidocket.com and credit lines.
Option a 63.0 to 63.433 s, final four samples including the last frame 1903. The credits card is unchanged through the final frame.

Option b 0.0 to 0.8 s. Same airport curb wide framing as option a: canopy, bench, suitcase, blue airport sign, phone overlay reading Ride requested, Finding a car. A white sensor-roofed SUV enters from the left and rolls right toward the chevron pickup bay. Caption Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a Waymo with no driver. These first samples look identical to option a.
Option b 1.0 to 1.8 s. The white SUV glides into the pickup bay and settles with a red glow at its rear lamp, phone still at Ride requested. Same composition as option a at this time.

Option b 2.0 to 2.8 s. The car holds in the bay while a Texas outline locator card fades in at top right. At 2.6 s a cut to the interior from behind the empty front seats: steering wheel, dash map screen and the airport sign through the windshield. Identical to option a at these samples.

Option b 3.0 to 3.8 s. Interior view: the steering wheel rotates with nobody in the empty front seats, the airport sign slides past the windshield's right edge, and the Texas locator outline draws. Same as option a at these samples.

Option b 4.0 to 4.8 s. Interior view held: steering wheel turned with its marker at right, seats empty, sign edge at the windshield border, locator outline complete. No visible change across these samples, matching option a.

Option b 5.0 to 5.8 s. Interior shot ends, caption clears, then at 5.4 s a closer curb shot shows a large tilted phone in front of the parked white SUV and the airport sign. The phone still reads Ride requested. Caption the airport included. Same as option a.
Option b 6.0 to 6.8 s. The phone route marker reaches the pin and the status changes from Ride requested to Arriving, At the curb at 6.2 s. Caption clears by 6.6 s. Same as option a.

Option b 7.0 to 7.8 s. Different from option a: a flat, straight-on square paper map with a grid fills the upper half against an olive backdrop, with three small pin circles near center, two pale green patches and a February calendar page pinned at its lower left. At 7.8 s a blue river segment and gray road lines begin to draw. Caption The service began in February. Lower half is plain olive.

Option b 8.0 to 8.8 s. On the flat map the blue river line extends from top to bottom while thin gray highways and a loop road draw around the three central pins. The Texas locator card fades out. February page stays at lower left. Lines are thin and pale at phone size.

Option b 9.0 to 9.8 s. The flat wall map holds, then at 9.4 s a cut puts the same map on a brown plank table in perspective with sky above; the February page has left the map. A 60 square miles, Limited area tag pins at the top and a February page slides in from the right to the lower right corner, while a black outline line starts tracing at upper left. From 9.4 s this matches option a's map-zone shot.

Option b 10.0 to 10.8 s. On the tabletop map the black outline traces clockwise from the top down the right side toward the pins while the February page settles at the lower left. Matches option a in these samples.

Option b 11.0 to 11.8 s. The black outline closes into an irregular polygon around the three pins and fills translucent gray, with the 60 square miles tag above and the February page at lower left. Matches option a.
Option b 12.0 to 12.8 s. The completed zone map holds; the small pins drift a few pixels, one leaving a faint short trail. Caption clears at 12.8 s. Matches option a.

Option b 13.0 to 13.8 s. Cut at 13.2 s to a straight-down overhead view: a brown creek band crosses the frame between pale wavy banks with round tree canopies on green ground. A small white car seen from above, with a dark circular roof sensor, sits at the lower bank edge in the brown water with faint wake lines trailing left. The car is small, about a quarter of frame width, and stays put across these samples. Caption In April, an empty Waymo was swept into Salado Creek.

Option b 14.0 to 14.8 s. Overhead creek view held. The small white car stays at the lower bank edge with faint wake lines; its position shifts only a few pixels. No visible sliding or rotation yet. Cabin windows dark; occupancy not readable from overhead.

Option b 15.0 to 15.8 s. In the overhead view the car rotates slightly and moves left off the bank edge with a curved wake. At 15.4 s a cut to an eye-level view: the white SUV sits half-submerged in wide brown water with a flat-topped tree behind; it tilts nose-down and drifts left with a bow wave on its right. This eye-level shot resembles option a's 15.4 s shot.

Option b 16.0 to 16.8 s. The car is sunk to the window line in the brown creek with a wave crest and debris trailing right; its screen position changes little. Dark rounded shapes show in the side windows. Car is small, roughly a quarter of frame width. Same picture as option a at these samples.

Option b 17.0 to 17.8 s. The submerged car drifts off the left edge. At 17.6 s a cut to the flooded residential street: white SUV in brown water before tan houses, a tree, fence and street sign, dark gray blob at right, sidewalk tiles below. Disclosure reads Another car, earlier in April. Same as option a.

Option b 18.0 to 18.8 s. The white SUV rolls slowly right along the flooded street while brown water rises up past its wheel arches. Caption Earlier that month, another empty car was stranded in floodwater. Same as option a.
Option b 19.0 to 19.8 s. The SUV stops in the flooded street and small amber lamps glow at its front and rear from 19.6 s. Same as option a.
Option b 20.0 to 20.8 s. Closer side view of the stopped SUV in brown floodwater with its reflection; amber corner lamps blink on and off. Windows show empty seat headrests. Same as option a.
Option b 21.0 to 21.8 s. Same close side view; the stopped car's corner lamps keep blinking, water and car hold still, seats empty. Same as option a.

Option b 22.0 to 22.8 s. Cut to a different framing from option a: a flat overhead brown desk panel on an olive background, with the cream Federal recall record card sliding in from the right edge and a pen at lower right. Field text starts typing Reca, Sof. The card is cropped at the right edge. Caption Waymo filed a software recall.

Option b 23.0 to 23.8 s. On the overhead desk the record card settles and types Recall type, Software, then Potential units affected, 3,791, with a cursor following. Same field content as option a, framed flat from above.

Option b 24.0 to 24.8 s. The completed card holds on the overhead desk, caption clears, then at 24.6 s the layout shifts to the card at top with an empty icon grid below, the same layout as option a. By 24.8 s three white car icons fill. Caption that could affect nearly thirty eight hundred cars.
Option b 25.0 to 25.8 s. The car icon grid fills row by row while a hand in a blue sleeve carries a wooden stamp in from the right over the card. Same as option a.

Option b 26.0 to 26.8 s. The full icon grid, the hand hovering the stamp, the Nearly 3,800 vehicles tag dropping in and straightening, and the stamp pressing an amber mark at 26.8 s. Same as option a.
Option b 27.0 to 27.8 s. The stamp lifts revealing Software recall on the card; the hand withdraws to the right; the card, tag and full grid hold. Same as option a.

Option b 28.0 to 28.8 s. After the record layout, at 28.4 s a cut to a top-down view of a straight two-lane road running vertically with grass verges. A small white car seen from above travels up the right lane. At 28.6 s the caption band overlaps the car's lower body. At 28.8 s a faint quote card fades in at the top. No water visible yet. Car is small, about a sixth of frame width.

Option b 29.0 to 29.8 s. Top-down road: the quote card is fully readable at top, the small white car stays at mid-lower frame while lane dashes scroll past it. A gray-blue water patch slides in from the top edge across the lane and grows from 29.2 s, partly behind the quote card. The car sits just above the caption band.

Option b 30.0 to 30.8 s. The gray-blue water patch moves down the road toward the car, its upper half hidden behind the quote card. The small car stays in place; at 30.8 s two tiny red brake marks appear at its rear, touching the top of the caption band. The water is still roughly a car length or more ahead of the car.

Option b 31.0 to 31.8 s. A large gray-blue water patch now fills the right lane above the car, its lower edge about half a car length ahead. The car shows red brake marks at its rear and holds position as lane dashes slow. The upper water is behind the quote card. Car sits directly above the caption band.

Option b 32.0 to 32.8 s. From above, the car creeps toward the gray-blue water edge, still a short gap away at 32.6 s. At 32.8 s a cut to an eye-level close side view of the SUV on the lane with the quote card above, matching option a's 32.8 s framing.

Option b 33.0 to 33.8 s. Close side view: a pale water patch slides in from the right edge toward the front tire while the car stays fixed. Caption then drive into standing water on higher speed roads. Same as option a.
Option b 34.0 to 34.8 s. The pale water sheet reaches the front tire and spreads under it with small splash marks; the word may lights amber. Same as option a.
Option b 35.0 to 35.8 s. The pale water sheet spreads under the car with fanned wakes at the front tire while the car body stays fixed on screen; may stays amber. Same as option a.
Option b 36.0 to 36.8 s. The car stands in the pale water sheet with wakes at both wheels as the background drifts left; caption clears at 36.6 s. Same as option a.
Option b 37.0 to 37.8 s. Cut to the tall record card; the Remedy row types The remedy is currently under development and lights pale amber. Same as option a.
Option b 38.0 to 38.8 s. A hand with a pen enters from the right and rests the pen tip at the end of the remedy text on the lit row. Same as option a.
Option b 39.0 to 39.8 s. With the pen resting on the remedy row, a second blue-sleeved arm brings a wooden stamp over the lower remedy row while the framing pushes in slightly. Same as option a.
Option b 40.0 to 40.8 s. The stamp presses onto the lower remedy row and lifts away leaving a tilted amber Under development mark; the pen hand stays. Same as option a.

Option b 41.0 to 41.8 s. The pen and stamp hands withdraw; caption clears. At 41.6 s a cut to the wet lot with four parked white cars, a wire, map card and April page; a tag partly reading ther limits slides in at 41.8 s. Same as option a.
Option b 42.0 to 42.8 s. The Weather limits, tightened tag slides along the wire and pins, gaining a cloud and rain icon; the four parked cars do not move. Same as option a.
Option b 43.0 to 43.8 s. The Weather limits tag moves to the wire's center and sways; the parked cars stay unchanged. Same as option a.
Option b 44.0 to 44.8 s. The lot holds with only a slight tag sway; parked cars, map card and April page unchanged. Same as option a.

Option b 45.0 to 45.8 s. The wide lot holds, caption clears, then at 45.6 s a closer low view of the car row with a larger Weather limits tag. Caption and every affected car had the update by April twentieth. Same as option a.
Option b 46.0 to 46.8 s. Check-mark badges pop above each car in turn from the front car toward the back. This page's image hash is identical to option a's page 046, so the pictures are the same.
Option b 47.0 to 47.8 s. All visible cars carry checks and the vehicle map card gains a small check, then the frame holds. Image hash is identical to option a page 047.
